speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what are the findings from the trial of using speed-tracking devices for heavy vehicles in 2018; and (b) whether there are plans to mandate speed-tracking devices for heavy vehicles to curb speeding.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: One limitation, however, is that the speed limiters can be tampered with.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They do not, therefore, confer significant advantages over speed limiters.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In addition, the cost to install the speed tracking devices is not low.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: TP will continue to require the use of speed limiters in heavy vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: TP will continue to monitor the development of other technologies that can help to discourage speeding.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: TP will also continue to adopt a multi-pronged strategy to getting heavy vehicle drivers to drive safely, including strict enforcement, sustained education and engagement.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My main concern really is that when there is an accident involving a heavy vehicle, the chance of fatality is very high, especially for those who are carrying a lot of people in the back.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The problem then is how are we going to tackle the people who are tampering with the speed limiters.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary or the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) consider increasing the penalties for those who tamper with the speed limiters?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second question is whether MHA will consider installing the speed counters that we have in our military vehicles.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can we consider putting those counters in our heavy vehicles?

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We will study whether we need to increase the penalties for tampering.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Just to share with the Member that it is an offence to tamper with a speed limiter installed in heavy vehicles.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: More severe punishment is meted out to those who are repeat offenders.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: There are also laws that ensure heavy vehicle owners maintain the speed limiters in proper working condition.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Again, there are penalties for failure to abide by this law.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: That said, we are not just stopping there.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We are also looking to enhance the punishment, in particular.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: Also, TP engages heavy vehicle drivers regularly through education, safety dialogues and various other sessions.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: On the use of the speed tracking devices, that is part of the trial.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: In fact, what we have tested in the trial were enhanced features where the business owners could actually track the speed of the vehicles when they are transmitted to the companies.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: So, the tracking device, as I have mentioned, can be tampered with, and tampering is something that is very difficult to detect.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: That is why we have quite serious punishments for it.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We will continue to study what we can do better.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: On a good note, the accidents involving heavy vehicles have, in fact, decreased.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: And the number of speeding-related accidents involving heavy vehicles decreased, too, by about 37% from 27 in 2014 to 17 in 2018.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: But nevertheless, we agree with the Member, one accident is still one too many.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
text: We will see what we can do better in this area.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: CLARIFICATION BY SENIOR PARLIAMENTARY SECRETARY TO THE MINISTER FOR EDUCATION

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Please allow me to respond to the earlier clarification by Dr Intan Mokhtar.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The child psychology clinic that she cited was reported by The New Paper in a 2010 article, and this child psychology clinic was just one of the initiatives that Temasek Polytechnic was considering.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This initiative was never implemented and Mr Brochez was not involved in this initiative.
